headline: Linux Eliminates strncpy API After Six Years of Work and 360 Patches
summary: The Linux kernel has officially removed the strncpy API after a lengthy development process involving hundreds of code patches. This move aims to enhance system security and stability.
details: The Linux kernel has completed the removal of the strncpy API, a process that spanned six years and required approximately 360 individual code patches. This significant undertaking reflects a long-term commitment to improving the security and reliability of the operating system.

The strncpy function, a string copying utility, has long been associated with potential buffer overflow vulnerabilities if not used with extreme care. Its removal is part of a broader effort within the Linux community to eliminate legacy code that poses security risks.

This extensive cleanup involved meticulous review and refactoring of code across the kernel to ensure that all instances of strncpy were replaced with safer alternatives. The sheer number of patches highlights the complexity of the task and the thoroughness of the development process.

While the exact date of the final removal in the mainline kernel was not specified, the completion of this multi-year effort signifies a major milestone in kernel development. Developers can now rely on more secure string manipulation functions, reducing the attack surface for potential exploits.

topic: tesla autopilot crash kills woman in texas
headline_marked: Tesla allegedly in autopilot mode [[crashes into Texas house, killing woman]]
headline: Tesla allegedly in autopilot mode crashes into Texas house, killing woman
summary: A driver in a Tesla Model 3 reportedly left the roadway and struck a residence, resulting in a fatality. The investigation is ongoing.
details: A fatal incident occurred in Katy, Texas, when a Tesla Model 3, allegedly operating with an automated driving assistance system, crashed into a home.
According to the Harris County Sheriff's office, the driver, Michael Butler, failed to maintain a single lane, veered off the roadway, and impacted the brick residence at high speed.
The vehicle entered the home, striking a resident identified as M. Avila, who was inside at the time. She was airlifted to a hospital but later pronounced dead.
The driver sustained injuries but showed no signs of intoxication and is cooperating with authorities. No charges have been filed as the investigation continues.
caption:
A Tesla operating on autopilot allegedly crashed into a Texas home, killing a resident inside. Investigators are looking into the incident.

A fatal incident occurred in Katy, Texas, when a Tesla Model 3, allegedly operating with an automated driving assistance system, crashed into a home.

According to the Harris County Sheriff's office, the driver, Michael Butler, failed to maintain a single lane, veered off the roadway, and impacted the brick residence at high speed.

The vehicle entered the home, striking a resident identified as M. Avila, who was inside at the time. She was airlifted to a hospital but later pronounced dead.

The driver sustained injuries but showed no signs of intoxication and is cooperating with authorities. No charges have been filed as the investigation continues.
